title: From Scattered Knowledge to a Club Playbook

nodes.label:
Undocumented
Know-How Exists
nodes.title: Documenting Club Procedures
nodes.info: Writing down how a specific recurring task is done -- setting up the room, running registration, closing down for the night -- at the moment someone first does it.

nodes.label:
Reducible
to Steps?
nodes.title: Reducible to Steps?
nodes.info: Some know-how is a fixed sequence; other know-how is a judgement call that resists being written as steps. Trying to force the second kind into an SOP produces a document nobody can follow.

nodes.label: Write as an SOP
nodes.title: Standard Operating Procedure
nodes.info: The specific formatted document that documenting-procedures work produces: a consistent template -- Purpose, Materials Needed, Steps, Troubleshooting -- applied every time.

nodes.label:
Transfer Through Shadowing
and Co-Leading
nodes.title: Knowledge Transfer Process
nodes.info: The deliberate techniques -- shadowing, co-leading, and structured handoff conversations -- used to move harder-to-write-down knowledge from one person's head into another's.

nodes.label:
Incoming Leader
Completes Onboarding
nodes.title: New Leader Onboarding
nodes.info: The structured sequence a designated successor works through before fully taking over: reviewing every written procedure and SOP, then shadowing and co-leading sessions.

nodes.label:
Filed in the Club
Playbook Document
nodes.title: Club Playbook Document
nodes.info: The single master document -- a shared folder or wiki with one clear table of contents -- assembling every piece into a binder a completely new lead could work from.

legend.text: Can it be written as steps?
